title: Neural Forecasting
interviewAnswer: Neural forecasting models learn temporal patterns across one or many series using recurrent, convolutional or transformer-style architectures. They are most useful when scale, many related series or rich covariates justify the complexity.
keyPoints: Always compare with strong statistical baselines.
Global models share information across series.
why: Neural Forecasting appears frequently in data-science work because it connects mathematical assumptions to practical decisions, diagnostics and failure modes.
intuition: Always compare with strong statistical baselines.
deepDive: Neural forecasting models learn temporal patterns across one or many series using recurrent, convolutional or transformer-style architectures. They are most useful when scale, many related series or rich covariates justify the complexity. Global models share information across series. Probabilistic objectives are common. A strong practitioner separates the modeling assumption from the estimation procedure, checks diagnostics rather than trusting a single score, and explains what would make the method inappropriate.
workedExample: Use a global neural model across thousands of products rather than one model per short series.
commonMistakes: Applying the method without checking its assumptions or data-generating process.
Choosing it because it is familiar rather than comparing against an appropriate baseline.
followUps: What assumptions does Neural Forecasting make?
How would you validate or debug Neural Forecasting in practice?
production: In production, validate assumptions on real data, monitor the quantities that can drift, and keep a simple baseline so added complexity has a measurable reason to exist.
